observed_title: On the duality gap and Gale’s example in conic linear programming

read_ranges.scope: Read complete paper.md in sequential ranges1–255,256–505,506–750: introduction and convex-analysis preliminaries, all Proposition1–2/Corollary3–5/Example4, Gale Lemma7/Proposition8, original ℓp example/domain/closure discussion and references. No appendix. PDF pages2,5,7,8,10,13 rendered: visually retained overbars erased by text extraction, corrected Example4 printed location, Gale definition and gap formula.

topic_relevance.B01: direct: conic weak/strong duality through the value function; exact duality gap and dual-attainment separation in perturbed Gale example.
topic_relevance.B02: adjacent: infinite sequence LP and infinitely indexed dual inequalities; finite-dimensional truncation is not justified as full separation.
topic_relevance.B04: direct: topology-dependent value-function lower semicontinuity, subdifferentiability and four precise qualification conditions; boundary counterexample.

definitions.name: Conic primal/dual and topology
definitions.statement: X,Y Hausdorff locally convex, A:X→Y continuous linear, c∈X*, b∈Y, P⊂X,Q⊂Y convex cones. Primal inf⟨x,c⟩ over x∈P,Ax−b∈Q; dual sup⟨b,y*⟩ over y*∈Q+,c−A*y*∈P+. Positive cones use≥0 pairing, X* and Y* are continuous topological duals.

definitions.name: Value function and lower semicontinuous envelope
definitions.statement: h_c(y)=inf{⟨x,c⟩:x∈P,Ax−y∈Q}; dom h_c=A(P)−Q. Its lower semicontinuous envelope is bar h_c, distinct from h_c. PDF2 and5 overbars are lost in paper.md; Proposition1(iv) says bar h_c is proper iff h_c* proper, NOT h_c proper iff dual feasible.

definitions.name: Intrinsic core
definitions.statement: icr E is the relative algebraic interior in aff E; Y0=span(A(P)−Q) carries its induced topology. icr, ambient int and relative int are not interchangeable without hypotheses.

definitions.name: Gale finite-sequence model
definitions.statement: X=R^(N) finite-support real sequences with convex-core topology τ_c, X*=R^N all sequences. P=nonnegative finite-support sequences,Q={0}, A x=(x0+Σ_{k≥1}k xk,Σ_{k≥1}xk). Its dual constraints are u≤c0,ku+v≤c_k for all k≥1.

theorem_cards.label: Proposition1: gap and dual attainment are separate
assumptions: Exact Hausdorff locally convex conic model and continuous A,c as defined.
Finite value h_c(b)∈R for the finite strong-duality equivalence.
theorem_cards.statement: Primal value=h_c(b), dual value=h_c**(b)≤h_c(b). At a finite value, lower semicontinuity at b is equivalent to equal finite primal/dual values; ∂h_c(b) nonempty is equivalent to equality plus dual attainment, and optimal dual solutions are precisely∂h_c(b). PDF(iv) concerns properness of bar h_c, not properness of unclosed h_c.
proof_steps: 作者证明：compute the conjugate of Φ_c and h_c as indicators of dual feasible sets (lines124–171), shift perturbation by b (lines181–200), then invoke [16]Theorem2.6.1 (lines227–241).
本次核验弱对偶：for feasible x,y*, ⟨x,c⟩−⟨b,y*⟩=⟨x,c−A*y*⟩+⟨Ax−b,y*⟩≥0.
本次核验：Fenchel equality identifies a supporting continuous affine minorant at b with an attained multiplier; continuity/lsc and subgradient existence remain separate concepts.
gaps: General biconjugate/subdifferential implications are imported convex-analysis results, not independently reproved here.
Text extraction loses overbars in preliminaries and1(iv); replacing bar h_c by h_c would create a false properness statement in general infinite-dimensional spaces.

theorem_cards.label: Proposition2 and Corollary3: four qualification routes
assumptions: Let Y0=span(A(P)−Q) with induced topology. At least one of the following four alternatives holds.
(i)For someλ0∈R, the feasible-value≤λ0 perturbations N0 form a neighborhood of b inY0.
(iii)X,Y are Fréchet spaces, P,Q,Y0 are closed and b∈icr(A(P)−Q).
Corollary3 separately endows real vector spaces X,Y with the convex-core topologies and assumes b∈icr(A(P)−Q).
theorem_cards.statement: Either h_c=−∞ throughout icr dom h_c and both values at b are−∞, or c∈P++A*(Q+), h_c restricted toY0 is continuous at b, values are equal and finite, and the dual is attained. If Y0=Y, dual optimum set is weak* compact.
proof_steps: 作者证明：apply [16]Theorem2.7.1 to shifted perturbation; under finite branch use continuous convex subgradient theorem, thenProposition1. Weak* compactness invokes [16]Theorem2.4.9. Corollary3 uses algebraic dual/convex-core subdifferentiability result [7].
本次核验：the finite branch is conditional; none of four CQ alternatives by itself excludes−∞ objective.
gaps: These are four alternatives, not a joint collection of assumptions. Weak* compactness additionally needsY0=Y.
Convex-core topology changes the continuous dual; its corollary cannot be transported to an arbitrary fixed norm topology.
The nonempty P interior alone does not place b in icr A(P); boundary counterexample remains.

theorem_cards.label: Corollary5: interior and boundary derivative route
assumptions: (c,b) belongs toΛ so primal and dual feasible.
OneProposition2 qualification holds; interior usesint_{Y0}dom h_c.
At a boundary point y∈dom h_c\int_{Y0}dom h_c the right directional derivative(h_c)′_+(y,·) must be proper.
theorem_cards.statement: h_c restricted toY0 is finite continuous on relative interior; at the specified boundary points proper directional derivative gives a nonempty subgradient and strong duality with dual attainment.
proof_steps: 作者证明：continuous convex-function facts for interior and [2]Proposition2.134(ii) for boundary derivative criterion.
核验边界：being on dom alone is insufficient; proper directional derivative is explicit extra input and cannot be dropped.
gaps: The full boundary derivative theorem is an external dependency; this reading does not independently establish it in every locally convex topology.

theorem_cards.label: Lemma7 and Proposition8: perturbed Gale gap and attainment
assumptions: Gale finite-support model with convex-core topology as above.
theorem_cards.statement: Unique primal feasible point isb1e0; primal=b1c0, dual supremum=b1ubar, gap=b1max{0,β0−βbar}. The baseline(u,v)is attained optimal ifmin{β0,βbar}=0; dual attained if0<β0<βbar. Ifβ0≥βbar>0, attainment iff inf_{k≥1}(βk−βbar k)>−∞ (a finite real infimum). In the interiorb1>b2>0, dual feasibilityc∈P++ImA* plusCQ(iv) yields zero gap and dual attainment.
proof_steps: 作者Lemma7：dual(u+β′,v′) feasibility iffv′≤v+inf_k(βk−β′k); this impliesβ′≤βbar, andβ′<βbar supplies a finite v′ by controlling the tail and finitely many initial indices.
作者Proposition8：upper bound on dualu′ ismin{c0,u+βbar}; approach it from below usingLemma7, obtaining sup and gap. At the limiting slope, finiteness of the intercept infimum determines attainment.

本次核验：βbar=∞ gives min{β0,βbar}=β0 andzero gap; theβ0≥βbar>0 branch necessarily has finiteβbar becauseβ0 is real. The gap and attainment statements require all infinitely many indices; finite sampled constraints do not verifyliminf or intercept tail.
gaps: Zero gap alone does not guarantee attained dual multiplier: β0=1,βk=k−sqrt(k),u=v=0 hasβbar=1,gap0 butinf(βk−k)=−∞.
βbar andubar overbars are visually confirmed onPDF10 and distinct fromβk,u.
This formula is specific toGale operator/support/topology, not a general conic gap formula.

theorem_cards.label: Remark9–10 and Section4: ℓp domain and closure diagnosis
assumptions: Original historical example proposesX=ℓp,1≤p<∞ andA x=(x0+Σn x_n,Σx_n).
Actual maximal domainD_A=X∩D0, whereD0={x:Σn x_n converges}; weighted absolute-sum domainD_A^a separately.
theorem_cards.statement: D_A is dense proper linear subspace; A is not defined on allℓp and its graph is not closed. With all displayed sums required finite andnonnegative sequences, the correctedC′ isC0∪C1 in(17), its closure is{η≥0,y1−1≤y2≤0}; intersection withL before closure requiresη≥1 butafter closureη≥0.
proof_steps: 作者证明：Abel test/domain inclusions, dense finite sequences and separation contradiction for nonclosed graph; constructC′ by two nonzero sequence coordinates and calculate closure.
本次核验更直接：x^(n)=e_n/n has||x^(n)||_p=1/n→0 andA x^(n)=(1,1/n)→(1,0)≠A0; eachx^(n) has finite support. Thus graph is not closed.

核验：historical full-space bounded/continuousA-adjoint setup is inapplicable. A densely defined unbounded operator can still have an adjoint on a restricted dual domain; do not export the author’s wording as a general statement that every nonclosed operator has no adjoint.
